stemBlocks.value: A sales representative earns a basic salary of $1 800 per week plus 5% commission on sales. In one week she made sales totalling $75 000. (a) Calculate the commission earned. (b) Calculate her total earnings for the week.
Think first: Commission is a percentage of sales, not of salary, so the $75 000 is the base.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p026-q33 from workbook page 26.

strategyBlocks.value: Find 5% of the total sales for the commission, then add the fixed basic salary.

finalAnswerBlocks.value: (a) Commission = $3 750  (b) Total earnings for the week = $5 550

whyThisWorks.value: A commission scheme pays a guaranteed basic plus a share of what the seller brings in, so the two parts have different bases and must be found separately. Taking 5% of the salary would reward the employee for existing rather than for selling. Adding the two gives gross earnings for the week.

commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Taking 5% of $1 800 instead of 5% of $75 000.
Avoid this: Giving $3 750 as the total earnings.

commonErrors.misconception: Treating the 5% as a deduction and subtracting it.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Treating the 5% as a deduction and subtracting it.

examTip.value: Identify what the percentage is of before calculating. In commission questions it is always the sales figure.
